truth.question: Is the orchard really of no particular scientific interest, as the survey says?
truth.statement: No. The orchard's notebooks run unbroken from 1911, kept by nine hands, and show the first bloom creeping eleven days earlier across the century, while a measurable frost pocket shapes the lower ground. The survey that dismissed the site rested on four short visits in the driest days of a dry August. The two missing war-year volumes were lent to the farming board in 1917 and never returned. The October bloom itself proved nothing: it was a question, answered by a century of attention.

late_october.text: It is the last week of October.

orchard_on_hill.text: An old apple orchard covers a hill slope, with a gate, a pond at the bottom and rows of trees.

bramley_blooming.text: The big Bramley apple tree at the top of the hill is covered in white blossom in late October, as if it were May.

other_trees_bare.text: Every other tree on the slope is bare.

jonah_at_orchard.text: Jonah is a boy who lives by the orchard and sees the October blossom.

ada.text: Ada is an old woman at the orchard whom Jonah goes to with news.

ada_writes_daily.text: Ada writes the day up in a ruled notebook in the shed every evening, and has since before Jonah was born.

shed_heater.text: The orchard shed has a paraffin heater that ticks, a single bulb on a wire, and smells of old paper.

ada_already_knew.text: Ada already knew about the October blossom and was not surprised.

hives_at_orchard.text: There are beehives along the south fence of the orchard.

notice_on_gate.text: A notice has appeared on the orchard gate, tied at all four corners.

notice_is_survey_summary.text: The notice on the gate is a typed summary of an early science survey of the site.

jonah_photographed_notice.text: Jonah photographed the notice in place on the gate, with the bare trees behind it.

notice_later_removed.text: The notice was later taken down, and Jonah's photo is the only picture anyone has of it in place.

notice_zip_tied.text: The notice is fixed to the gate with zip-ties.

notebooks_go_back_decades.text: Ada's notebooks record blossom, frost and picking dates going back decades.

no_october_bloom_before.text: Nothing in Ada's records matches this October bloom.

loose_sheet_1952.text: A loose sheet in the 1952 notebook, written by Ada's mother, lists every strange thing the orchard has ever done.

six_shelves_1911.text: Six shelves of notebooks in the shed run unbroken from 1911 to the present, a hundred and fourteen years.

nine_hands.text: Nine different people have written in the notebooks over the years.

no_index.text: The notebooks have no index, list or key.

ada_sixty_years.text: Ada has written the day up every evening for sixty years.

ada_doubts_notebooks.text: Ada does not believe the notebooks, being only weather, can change anything.

ada_since_twenty_one.text: Ada began writing at twenty-one because her mother and grandmother did it before her.

ada_uneasy_weapon.text: Ada is uneasy about her notebooks being used as a weapon against a developer.

ada_names_eight.text: Ada can name eight of the nine hands; the ninth, a neat pencil from 1939 to 1943, is unknown to her.

oldest_notebooks_top_shelf.text: The oldest notebooks sit on the top shelf of the shed, their spines faded grey.

hard_1920s_hand.text: The 1920s handwriting is so slanted and faded that a three and a five look almost the same.

hands_four_periods.text: The nine hands sort into four periods, with changeovers falling in the same three months of different years.

volume_1911_first_bloom.text: The 1911 volume opens with the price of ladders and a first bloom date of April the fourteenth.

notebook_at_archive_desk.text: The 1911 notebook is taken out of the shed and laid open on the archive desk.

ada_never_let_notebook_leave.text: Ada has never let a notebook leave the shed in sixty years.

missing_1917_1918.text: The 1917 and 1918 volumes are missing from the shelf, and have been for a very long time.

other_buildings.text: The hill also has an old packing shed, a stone bothy used as a home in the war, and a garage loft.

father_lost_half_hill.text: Ada's father once signed a contract that lost him half the hill.

ada_signature_last.text: Ada will sign the objection only when it is ready: the signature is the last thing.

horse_taken_1917.text: Ada's gran told one war story: the army took the orchard horse in 1917 and brought it back in 1919.

ada_kindness_after.text: Ada says the hard part of speaking in rooms is the kindness afterwards.

ada_understands_ledger.text: Ada understands the spreadsheet once Tobe calls it a ledger like her father's shop accounts.

bees_active_october.text: The orchard bees are out and working in October, tricked by the warmth.

mrs_cassar_beekeeper.text: Mrs Cassar is a local beekeeper of thirty years who has never seen bees do this in October.

cassar_hive_records.text: Mrs Cassar keeps thirty years of her own hive records in notebooks.

count_mismatch.text: Mrs Cassar's bee count and Jonah's differ by more than half, and neither knows who counted wrong.

cassar_method_changes.text: Mrs Cassar changed her counting method in 2005 and 2014, so her earlier numbers are rough.

cassar_carrier_bags.text: Mrs Cassar brings her hive records to the shed in two carrier bags and refuses to have her rough counts dressed up as exact.

cassar_three_blocks.text: Mrs Cassar's dated method changes turn her thirty years into three clean, explainable blocks.

cassar_frame.text: Mrs Cassar keeps a perfect honeycomb frame in a glass case, kept since 2008, to show at the hearing.

cassar_swarm_story.text: Mrs Cassar tells Jonah a long story about a 1994 swarm while the panel decides.

survey_exists.text: An ecological survey of the orchard site has been written.

survey_dated_august.text: The survey is dated in August.

eleven_words.text: The survey's key sentence, eleven words long, says the site is of no particular scientific interest.

survey_signed_faulks.text: The survey is signed by D. Faulks.

faulks_name_noted.text: Jonah wrote the name D. Faulks in the back of his exercise book.

august_orchard_looks_like_nothing.text: In August the old orchard looks like nothing much: long grass, shade, weeds and duckweed.

survey_four_visits.text: The survey rests on four short dry-weather visits in August totalling under four hours.

developer_plan_exists.text: A developer wants to build on the orchard.

plan_82_houses.text: The plan is eighty-two homes and a spine road running straight along the row where the big Bramley stands.

brochure_village_hall.text: The developer left a glossy brochure of the plan in the village hall.

objection_process.text: The plan can be objected to through the council.

six_week_window.text: Objections to the plan close in six weeks.

objection_form_asks_proof.text: The council objection form asks for proof of scientific interest, the same phrase the survey used.

photo_date_stamp_october.text: The photo's date stamp shows the notice went up in October, cutting the objection window short.

survey_data_request.text: Jonah formally requested the survey's raw data and got a reference number.

foi_twenty_days.text: The developer must hand over the survey data within twenty working days, four weeks of the six.

survey_data_arrived.text: The survey's raw data arrives as a thin PDF: four visits, one line across the slope.

survey_species_list.text: The survey listed only twenty-two plant species.

survey_site_dry.text: The survey data notes that the site was dry at the time.

survey_in_drought.text: Public Met Office rain records show the four survey visits fell in the driest days of a dry August.

faulks_pattern.text: Faulks has other reports that always matched what the client wanted.

faulks_method_sound_timing_wrong.text: Faulks says his method was standard and sound, only done in the wrong two weeks.

timing_made_survey_useless.text: The case is not that Faulks did wrong but that poor timing made the survey nearly useless.

tobe.text: Tobe runs the school weather club and is delighted by a century of bloom dates.

tobe_laptop.text: Tobe owns a laptop that works, used for the copying.

city_archive.text: The city archive keeps records and offers a place for old papers.

archive_tuesday_desk.text: The city archive keeps a Tuesday desk where people bring in their papers.

mrs_okonkwo_archivist.text: Mrs Okonkwo is the archivist at the city archive.

dr_abara.text: Dr Ines Abara is a university scientist in long term monitoring.

abara_long_series_rare.text: Dr Abara says a long unbroken local series is truly rare.

abara_method_everything.text: Dr Abara says the series is only evidence if its method and observers can be shown.

abara_walked_rows.text: Dr Abara walked the orchard rows for two hours in the rain.

abara_two_pages_condition.text: Dr Abara will write two pages on cold air drainage only if six weeks of dawn readings are taken.

abara_why.text: Dr Abara returned Jonah's first method draft with one word: why.

abara_will_read_once.text: Dr Abara will read the dossier once and decide whether to put her name near it.

abara_report.text: Dr Abara wrote a report that used the phrase long unbroken local series.

abara_attends.text: Dr Abara will attend the hearing and say only what she can defend.

raval_at_council.text: Priya Raval works at the council.

raval_asks_method.text: Priya Raval, the council ecology officer, says data needs a stated method, a keeper or chain of care, and a way to check it.

raval_not_ready.text: Raval says the notebooks are useful but not ready to be proof.

raval_can_explain_rules.text: Raval cannot help an objector but may explain what the board will look for.

halvor_coffee.text: Halvor bought Jonah a coffee that Jonah did not drink.

halvor_asks_what_stops.text: Halvor asked Jonah what would make him stop.

nothing_would_stop_jonah.text: The honest answer to Halvor is that nothing would make Jonah stop.

editor_carver.text: The local paper's editor is Carver, thirty years at the paper.

newspaper_offer.text: The local paper offers to run a story with a photo of Ada and the notebooks.

jonah_mother.text: Jonah's mother signs the trust papers without pause.

jonah_copied_eleven_words.text: Jonah copied the eleven words into the back of his exercise book.

jonah_counted_trees.text: Jonah's count of the orchard trees comes out differently each time.

forty_thousand_lines.text: The whole record is about forty thousand daily lines, too many for six weeks.

four_lines_a_year.text: Typing only four dates a year gives four hundred and fifty-six numbers instead of forty thousand lines.

four_dates_defined.text: The four dates are first bloom, full bloom, last frost and first picking.

spreadsheet_set_up.text: Tobe sets up a spreadsheet with four columns and a hundred and fourteen rows.

photograph_every_page.text: Every typed page is photographed so any number can be checked against the original.

photo_technique.text: Jonah learns to photograph pages without his shadow falling on the numbers.

extension_lead_laptop.text: The laptop runs on the shed bench from an extension lead out to the house.

pond_flat_spot.text: The only flat spot in the orchard is by the pond.

ada_reads_1920s_aloud.text: Ada reads the 1920s pages aloud while Jonah types.

work_is_late_nights.text: Ada says the work is mostly late nights, cold fingers and feeling it is not enough.

school_hall_thursdays.text: The school hall is free on Thursdays and the caretaker agrees to lend it.

archive_checks_in_person.text: The archive will not take anything it cannot see and check in person.

bloom_chart_made.text: Tobe charts the bloom dates against the years.

bloom_eleven_days_earlier.text: Across the century the first bloom date moved eleven days earlier in a steady creep.

bramley_row_case.text: A Bramleys-only record is fewer numbers and simple to explain.

class_could_type.text: Thirty pairs of hands could type the century in a fortnight but could add many errors.

one_error_risk.text: A single wrong date could let the whole chart be questioned.

archive_offer.text: Mrs Okonkwo offers a stable-temperature, north-facing locked room, a receipt and Ada's right to see the notebooks.

double_typing_eleven_mismatches.text: Two people typed every page separately and the comparison found eleven mismatches in a hundred pages.

nineteen_marked_unclear.text: Nineteen unreadable figures out of four hundred and fifty-six are marked with question marks, not guessed.

frost_pocket.text: A low dip by the pond is a frost pocket where cold air settles; the big Bramley stands above it.

class_typing_in_hall.text: Thirty people type up the century in the school hall on Thursday afternoons.

class_done_1930s.text: The school class finished typing the 1930s.

chart_on_shed_door.text: The printed bloom chart is pinned to the shed door, where passers-by stop to look.

council_corridor_wait.text: Jonah waited forty minutes in a council corridor with a recycling poster and a vending machine.

list_1948_1953.text: Ada's mother's list records a November bloom in 1948 and a June frost in 1953.

odd_events_pattern_is_proof.text: Dr Abara agrees that a written pattern of odd events is itself proof.

custody_note.text: Mrs Okonkwo writes a custody note recording where every volume has been.

four_objections_listed.text: Tobe lists four objections Faulks could make: not continuous, untrained observers, inconsistent method, unchecked data.

method_section_needed.text: The objection needs a written method section explaining how the record was kept and checked.

method_section_written.text: Jonah has written the method section of the dossier.

frost_readings_done.text: Dawn thermometer readings in the frost pocket and at the hilltop run for six weeks.

two_thermometers_used.text: Two thermometers are used from the start, one in the frost pocket and one at the hilltop.

only_one_thermometer_before.text: Until a second thermometer is bought for eleven pounds, the frost study relies on one.

blue_notebook.text: The readings go into a new blue notebook bought in town.

frost_pocket_four_degrees.text: The frost pocket is up to four degrees colder than the hilltop.

tobe_nineteen_of_42.text: Tobe did nineteen of the forty-two dawn readings without complaint.

frost_chart.text: A chart of the frost pocket readings is made.

frost_chart_on_door.text: The frost pocket chart is pinned beside the bloom chart on the shed door.

letters_to_families.text: Four of the nine writers have living family in the city, and Jonah writes to them.

letters_posted.text: Jonah posted the four letters to the writers' families.

parish_records_archive.text: The parish records are kept in the same archive as the notebooks.

parish_box_1917.text: Mrs Okonkwo brings Jonah the 1917 parish box in the reading room.

volumes_lent_1917.text: A parish receipt shows two orchard books were lent to the farming board in August 1917 for the war effort and not returned.

farming_board_successor.text: The farming board's successor keeps an office with a basement in the old market building.

card_index_1961.text: The basement holds a card index of the board's items that stops in 1961, under a four-minute light timer.

volumes_found.text: Jonah finds the two missing war-year books undamaged in a box marked WAR COMMITTEE MISC in the basement.

war_volume_horse_line.text: The war volumes are ordinary, with one line from September 1917 about the horse.

ada_adds_fourteen.text: Ada adds fourteen species from memory, making thirty-six, but will not swear to them until spring.

species_need_may.text: A proper species list needs a trained walk in May; it is now November.

nine_species_sure.text: Walking the rows in November, Jonah can be sure of only nine species.

dawn_rota.text: A rota of names on the shed door organises the dawn readings.

orchard_trust.text: The Orchard Hill Trust is set up with the signatures of Ada, Mrs Cassar and Jonah's mother to hold the data and make the objection.

hearing_scheduled.text: The objection will be heard at a council hearing in a room of about forty people.

public_hearing.text: A public hearing would make Faulks answer questions out loud.

ada_page_to_read.text: Ada will choose one notebook page to read aloud at the hearing.

ada_read_1947_page.text: Ada read a March 1947 page at the hearing about ice and a cold snap blackening the early blossom.

dossier_numbered.text: Every page of the dossier is numbered and every figure sourced.

release_timing_dilemma.text: Releasing the dossier early lets the builder's experts pick at it; late looks like a trick.

ada_tobe_disagree.text: Ada and Tobe disagree about handing the dossier to the developer before the hearing.

objection_submitted.text: The objection goes in with the data, method, custody note, nine species and a new eleven-word covering line.

war_books_in_record.text: The found war books and their receipt go into the record as proof of its care.

panel_hearing_held.text: The hearing is held before a council panel and its chair.

rainfall_sheet_answers.text: Tobe's single sheet of survey dates over August rainfall answers why the survey should not stand.

amateur_answered.text: When a panel member calls the notebooks amateur, Jonah answers with the custody note, double-typing and marked doubts.

jonah_admits_short.text: Jonah tells the panel that six weeks of frost readings is short before anyone else can.

file_shared_all.text: Jonah sends the dossier to the panel, the builder and the public on the same day.

hearing_ran_late.text: The hearing ran an hour late, through a drainage item and a fence dispute.

charts_on_easel.text: The two charts stand on an easel all afternoon before the orchard item is called.

phrase_in_minutes.text: The note-taker writes long unbroken local series into the official minutes.

panel_held_frame.text: Every panel member handles Mrs Cassar's honeycomb frame.

eight_seconds_silence.text: After Ada's reading nobody speaks for eight seconds.

officer_report.text: The officer's report drops the no-interest wording and cites the long records, frost data and species list.

conditions_set.text: Conditions are set: a May resurvey by a fresh ecologist, a full-winter frost study, and the records lodged with the archive.

road_move_option.text: The spine road could be moved forty metres east, for a price.

three_homes_choice.text: The notebooks could go to the archive, the trust, or stay in the shed.

letter_to_class.text: Jonah writes the class an honest letter of thanks that does not pretend the orchard is safe.

jonah_answer_process.text: Jonah tells Halvor that what would make him stop now is a fair process, not giving in.

winter_needs_nine_people.text: A full winter of dawn readings needs nine people, a spare thermometer and someone for December.

ada_teaches_hands.text: Ada teaches young volunteers to read the nine hands.

trust_purpose_written.text: After four meetings the trust's purpose is written down and signed.

someone_must_write_daily.text: Someone must take over writing the day up every evening in the shed.

may_resurvey_61_species.text: The May resurvey found sixty-one species, including an orchid never recorded on the hill.

resurvey_report_watched.text: The resurvey report says the orchard should be watched, not cleared.

jonah_sent_bad_letter.text: Jonah sent one letter he should not have sent.

ada_tired.text: After four months Ada is more tired and her writing shakier.

record_continued_after_october.text: The notebook record carries on being written after the October bloom.

record_stopped.text: Nobody wrote in the notebooks after Ada's entry on the evening of the October bloom.

jonah_accused_faulks.text: Jonah publicly claimed that Faulks shaped the survey for the builder, without proof.

case_made_honestly.text: Looking back, almost all the work stands; the blame of Faulks is the one thing Jonah would take back.

april_normal_bloom.text: In April the whole row blooms on time, and the October bloom does not happen again.

road_moved_east.text: The spine road is moved forty metres east, around the top of the hill, and the Bramley row stands.

plaque_offer.text: The builder offers a saved corner, a sign and a plaque with Ada's name, excluding the Bramley row.

window_closed_unused.text: The objection window closed without the notebooks being used.

tried_everything_failed.text: Trying to type everything, Jonah finished only twelve years before exhaustion.

notebooks_catalogued_archive.text: The notebooks are catalogued at the archive but never used; a resurvey by the same method gives the same result.

chart_corrected_trust_harmed.text: The unchecked chart came back with a correction and Jonah's trust was harmed.

chart_admired_filed.text: The chart, sent without method, was admired and filed while the window ran out.

three_wrong_guesses.text: Faulks found three guessed dates and the whole chart was treated as guesses.

photo_ran_page_five.text: The paper ran Ada's photo on page five, people shared it, and the deadline passed.

jonah_lost_trust.text: After Jonah's unprovable claim about Faulks, nothing he said was trusted.

file_online_four_hundred.text: The unchecked file went online, four hundred people read it, and no one with power answered.

data_returned_no_method.text: Raval returned the numbers because they had no stated method.

argument_about_jonah.text: After the published charge, the fight became about Jonah instead of the orchard.

found_secret.text: Jonah quietly put the found books back on the shelf and told no one where they had been.

dossier_sent_incomplete.text: With no release date chosen, the deadline sent in an unfinished dossier.

faulks_file_sent.text: Jonah attached the file and sent it, letting the facts speak.

objection_accepted_resurvey_may.text: The objection is accepted on its evidence and the survey must be redone in May.

record_copied_lodged.text: The copied record is lodged with the archive, open to anyone, and no longer fragile.

chain_of_people.text: Jonah sees the notebooks are about a chain of people showing up for a hundred and fourteen years.

chair_careful_lost.text: Jonah answered a fair question as unfair and the decision went against the orchard.

six_answers_honest_no.text: Jonah answered six questions with proof and honestly declined a seventh; a new growing-season survey was asked for.

deed_of_gift.text: The notebooks go to the archive under a deed of gift with Ada's lasting right to read them.

developer_funds_five_years.text: The developer must fund five years of winter frost checks, with the data belonging to the trust.

bloom_a_question_not_signal.text: Dr Abara says the bloom was not a signal but a question, answered by a century of attention.

jonah_writes_115th_year.text: Jonah writes up the day in a new notebook in his own hand, beginning the hundred and fifteenth year.

eleven_days_gap.text: The December readings stopped for eleven days over Christmas, leaving a gap in the winter series.

orchard_watched_series_public.text: The orchard is watched and the series is public and growing.

record_reason_to_be_believed.text: Jonah understands a record is not proof but the reason a person can be believed.

jonah_indexed_shelves.text: Jonah spends a year making the first index of the six shelves.

next_october_no_bloom.text: The next October the Bramley does not bloom and the picking is ordinary.

eleven_words_answered.text: The eleven words were not beaten but answered by the record.

ada_writes_new_notebook.text: Ada keeps writing, now in a new notebook.

second_thermometer_bought.text: A second thermometer is bought for eleven pounds so the frost study can survive a failure.

halvor_question_named_surveyor.text: Knowing the surveyor's name lets Jonah ask Halvor whether the builder ordered an August survey on purpose.

oddities_bunch_mild_winters.text: Ada's mother's list shows the orchard's oddities bunch in mild-winter or late-spring years.

photo_added_to_file.text: Tobe adds the photo of the notice to the file as evidence.

n00c0.event: In late October Jonah finds the big Bramley at the top of the bare orchard in full white blossom.

n01d0.event: Ada, writing up the day in the shed, says she already knows about the blossom; Jonah weighs three ways to start.

n02c0.event: Ada searches decades of her notebooks, finds no match, and Jonah spots her mother's loose list of strange events in the 1952 book.

n02c1.event: The south-fence hives are loud and working in October; Mrs Cassar later says she has never seen it in thirty years.

n02c2.event: A typed survey summary has been tied to the orchard gate; Jonah reads it twice and photographs it in place.

n03d0.event: Jonah faces six shelves of unindexed notebooks from 1911, written by nine hands, and must choose where to start.

cq_plant_did_find_who_wrote.event: Jonah finds the survey signed D. Faulks, dated August, and writes the name in his exercise book.

n03d1.event: At her kitchen table Mrs Cassar's bee count and Jonah's disagree by more than half, and neither can say who is wrong.

n03d2.event: Jonah reads the August survey summary at the gate; its eleven words call the site of no particular scientific interest.

n04d0.event: The survey is signed D. Faulks in August, when the orchard looks like nothing much; Jonah wonders what Faulks saw.

n04d1.event: The survey's method lists four dry visits of under an hour each across a fortnight in August.

n04d2.event: Ada says the notebooks are only weather and cannot change anything; Jonah cannot prove her wrong.

n04c0.event: Jonah copies the eleven words into the back of an exercise book at the kitchen table and carries them with him.

n04c1.event: In the dim shed Jonah runs a finger along the faded oldest notebooks on the top shelf.

n04c2.event: Jonah walks the rows counting trees and gets a different total each time.

n04c3.event: Ada names eight of the nine hands; the ninth, a pencil from 1939 to 1943, is a mystery.

n04c4.event: Jonah photographs the zip-tied notice; the photo later proves to be the only one of it in place.

n05d0.event: The council objection form, due in six weeks, asks for proof of scientific interest, mirroring the survey's phrase.

n05d1.event: The four survey visits add up to under four hours, on which a sentence could bring eighty-two houses and a road through the Bramley row.

n05d2.event: Mrs Okonkwo at the city archive's Tuesday desk hears Jonah out and says only: show me what you have.

n05d3.event: Jonah finds Dr Ines Abara, a university scientist in long term monitoring, and feels someone might understand.

n05d4.event: The developer's brochure shows eighty-two homes and a spine road aimed straight along the Bramley's row.

n05d5.event: Tobe, who runs the school weather club, grins at a century of bloom dates and opens his laptop.

e05_0.event: The six weeks pass in ordinary days and the window closes with nothing done.

n06d0.event: Tobe estimates forty thousand daily lines, far too many for six weeks.
